public_rationale: The April records support the limited claim that coding agents were not generally sufficient by themselves. A contemporary coding evaluation retained substantial failures, and a production incident required human recovery work. The same release evidence shows major advances, so this assessment does not deny useful autonomous coding or claim that every task needs continuous supervision.
limitations: General sufficiency is inferred from bounded evaluations and deployment evidence.
No evidence here establishes that human involvement will remain necessary indefinitely.
Marcus's characterization of Amodei's intentions is outside this assessment.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that contemporary coding agents do not generally replace skilled engineering oversight across software creation, maintenance, and operational safeguards.
This does not deny that agents can complete substantial individual tasks autonomously.
Use April 1–27, 2026, the current month through publication, for the ongoing capability claim.
Assess the sufficiency claim, not whether Amodei intended the position Marcus attributes to him.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations and deployment records show material engineering tasks or operational failures that agents do not reliably handle without human engineering support.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative production deployments and evaluations establish that agents alone reliably perform architecture, implementation, maintenance, and operational safeguards across ordinary software work.
